growth_problem.statement: The growth problem in Egypt is not a growth collapse: growth is 2.6 percent a year, 1.2 standard deviations above the convergence expectation (structural-peer median 1.2); the question is whether it is sustained and reaching the poor (inclusion is not assessed in the prototype). GDP per capita growth over 2016–2025 averaged 2.6 percent a year (2006–2025: 2.4; structural-peer median 1.2), 1.2 standard deviations above the convergence expectation and ranked 4 of 11 among structural peers. GDP per capita is at its peak to date (2025). Investment (gross fixed capital formation to GDP) is 1.8 standard deviations below expectation given income at 12.8 percent of GDP; the private-public split is unavailable in prototype (IMF Investment and Capital Stock Dataset not ingested). Gross savings is 1.4 standard deviations below expectation given income; the current account balance is -4.2 percent of GDP and net FDI inflows are 6.2 percent of GDP. Structural change (G9) is not computed in the prototype. Exports to GDP is 0.7 standard deviations below expectation given income, and economic complexity is 0.7 standard deviations below expectation (the complexity gap). The relevant question is therefore: whether current growth can be sustained and what would make it reach more of the population. Provisional top-split reading: low demand for investment (real lending rate t = -2.2, real private credit growth 3.2 percent, investment t = -1.8).

top_split.label: low demand for investment
top_split.reading: Low demand for investment; left branch (low returns)

structural.rule: structural: 10 nearest by Euclidean distance in z-scores of log_gdppc_ppp, log_population, resource_rents (diagonal Mahalanobis), with a landlocked mismatch adding 1 to the squared distance (one sd of a continuous feature); micro-states below 300000 excluded; high-income economies excluded; fragile and conflict-affected economies excluded; candidates with an income observation before 2023 excluded

regional.rule: regional: same region (Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan); income groups within 0 step(s) of Lower middle income until at least 6; capped at 15 nearest by log GDP per capita (PPP)

aspirational.rule: aspirational: GDP per capita (PPP) in 2000 within ±30% of the target's current 16918 and average growth since ≥ 3% a year; up to 10 by growth
